Below is a concise “tool‑kit” of the most reliable, production‑ready techniques that are used in modern game‑development pipelines for 3‑D spatial reasoning.  The methods are grouped by the operation you asked about, each with a short description, a recommended implementation approach (library or engine API), and a couple of inline references that you can follow up on (all URLs are current as of 2024).

---

## 1. 3‑D Coordinate Reasoning & Conventions  

| Topic | Practical approach | Why it’s reliable | References |
|-------|-------------------|-------------------|------------|
| **Right‑handed vs. left‑handed** | Most game engines (Unity, Unreal, Godot) use a **right‑handed** world space where *Y* is up, *X* points right, *Z* points backward (into the screen). Keep all imported assets in this space; convert only when you need a different view (e.g., camera‑space). | Consistent sign conventions eliminate accidental flip bugs in lighting, normals, and physics. | Unity – “Coordinate Systems”: <https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/CoordinateSystem.html> (2023) |
| **Local vs. global frames** | Store positions in **local space** for object‑relative calculations (e.g., attachment points) and transform to world space only for broad‑phase queries. Use the matrix stack `M = T * R * S` (translate‑rotate‑scale) – multiplication order matters. | Reduces floating‑point drift and makes debugging easier (you can inspect local transforms in editor). | Unreal Engine 5 Docs – “Transforms and Coordinates”: <https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.2/en-US/transforms-and-coordinates-in-unreal-engine/> (2023) |
| **Homogeneous coordinates** | Represent points as `(x, y, z, 1)` and vectors as `(x, y, z, 0)`. This lets you apply translation, rotation, and perspective in a single matrix multiply and cleanly distinguishes points from directions. | Guarantees correct behaviour for operations like ray‑origin vs. direction and for perspective division. | OpenGL GLSL spec – “4‑D vectors”: <https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec46.core.pdf> (2021) |

---

## 2. Transform Mathematics  

| Operation | Recommended method | Library / API | Key points |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------|------------|
| **Matrix construction (TRS)** | `M = Translate(T) * Rotate(R) * Scale(S)` where `Rotate` is a **quaternion‑to‑matrix** conversion. | Unity `Matrix4x4.TRS`, Unreal `FMatrix::MakeFromTranslationRotationScale`, **GLM** `glm::translate * glm::rotate * glm::scale` | Keep the order; avoid matrix‑matrix inversion for runtime (use `inverse` only when needed). |
| **Quaternion rotation** | Use **Slerp** for smooth interpolation: `q = Quaternion.Slerp(a, b, t)`. For short‑interval snapping use **Ln‑SLerp** or **Power‑Spline**. | Unity `Quaternion`, Unreal `FQuat::Slerp`, **Math.NET** `Quaternion.Slerp` | Quaternions avoid gimbal lock and are cheap for interpolation. |
